# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 18 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 18 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_018_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 3, Chapter 10

**1** She showed me a multitude of people coming from afar, and in the middle of them a man of great height, taller than the tower, with the appearance of a master of a large estate, with a great crown on his head and dressed in a gleaming white garment. **2** He had on his feet white boots; he had a sickle in his right hand and a shepherd's crook in his left. He came and took up his position in front of the tower. **3** He commanded the stones to be carried and fitted into the building. Six young men who were building and four others on his right hand carried the stones and built the building. **4** He then commanded the other men who were carrying stones to reject them all and throw them far from the tower. But not one stone was rejected that was near the tower; they were all placed in the building because they were smooth and bright. **5** But many were rejected from the large number that was far away. The man commanded them to be piled in heaps separately for themselves: some in one heap, some in another, some in another. But the twelve mountains were not piled up but were put in order according to their appearance. **6** After the stones had been placed in the building, the man called me and said: "Come to me, Hermas." I went to him and said, "Lord, do you command me?" He said: "What do you want to know?" "Lord," I said, "I wish to understand the meaning of this whole vision from the beginning to the end, and I wish to ask you concerning the stones which were placed in the building, concerning those which were rejected and thrown away, and why the building has not yet been completed."

---

*EMET note: The tall man with crown, sickle, and crook is the pre-eminent figure of this vision — likely representing Christ as Lord of the harvest and shepherd. The sickle echoes Rev 14:14-19.*
